rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for an object that is worn out, weathered, or in rough condition.

example.english: This table has been used for so many years and looks really battered.
example.traditional: 呢張枱用咗咁多年，睇落真係好殘舊。
example.jyutping: ni1 zoeng1 ci4 jung6 zo2 gam3 do1 nin4 tai2 lok6 zan1 hai6 hou2 caan4 gau6

rows.jyutping: bei2 jan4 daa2 dou3 zau1 san1 soeng1
rows.note: Use this for a person who has been physically beaten and is covered in injuries, rather than for a worn-out object.

example.english: They were battered and covered in injuries and had to go to hospital.
example.traditional: 佢畀人打到周身傷，入咗院。
example.jyutping: keoi5 bei2 jan4 daa2 dou3 zau1 san1 soeng1 jap6 zo2 jyun2

rows.note: Use this when describing someone who is visibly drunk or inebriated.

example.english: They came home after drinking, completely battered.
example.traditional: 佢飲完酒返到屋企，成個人醉醺醺。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jam2 jyun4 zau2 faan2 dou3 uk1 kei2 sing4 go3 jan4 zeoi3 fan1 fan1
